`f(n) = min{ m : n! = ∏_{a∈S} a, S ⊂ (n,m], |S|≥1, all distinct, m ∈ S }`.

Feasibility of a given m reduces exactly to subset-product: pool `P(n,m) = {d : n < d ≤ m, d | n!}` (every a_i must divide n!, since a_i | n! · (rest)^{-1}... more precisely each a_i is n!-smooth and a_i | n! because the complementary product is integral). Enumerate P(n,m) by scanning d ∈ (n,m] and testing d | n! via the prime factorization of n! (exponent of p in n! = Σ⌊n/p^j⌋). Feasibility = decide whether some subset of P(n,m) containing m has product exactly n! — done as exact subset-sum on prime-exponent vectors (dimension = π(n)), pruning: partial product must divide n!. Then f(n) = min feasible m over divisors m of n! with m > n, scanning upward. No floating point anywhere; all certificates are integer subsets S.
